chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: "A-Tisket, A-Tasket" as Ella's own idea; hiring Van Alexander
summary: The song was Ella's nursery-rhyme number; Van Alexander, hired as pop arranger, wrote it down.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: 'A Tisket A Tasket' was Ella's own thing. It was her own idea -- She would That was her thing that (inaudible) sing up in Yonkers or White Plains or wherever she was from. 'A Tisket A Tasket', that's a nursery rhyme. Her and some school kids would do, you know.
That was her own thing. We didn't put nothing -- we had nothing to do with that. We called Van to put it down on paper for her and Van made the arrangements.
I had hired Van, because I say, 'Chick,

we need an arranger for Ella," because this pop stuff was coming in.
So he used to come up to the Savoy and asked for a job -- asked Chick for a job. Chick say, "Well, bring in a couple of things."
He brought in a couple of arrangements, sound pretty good. So we assigned him to do some pop things with Ella. He came out all right.
